spark_scene.description: True-color satellite view of the main Hawaiian Islands with extensive white cloud cover over the northern islands and over the large island in the southeast, with dark open ocean visible to the southwest and south-central. No distinct haze or plume separable from ordinary cloud is visible.

firms.source: Kahu Ola /api/firms/hotspots?include_volcanic=1 (VIIRS NOAA-20/21 NRT, rolling 24 h)
firms.volcanic_note: summit-caldera thermal detections (active vent glow), excluded from fire clusters

adp.note: Satellite haze estimate, not an official product. ADP cannot tell wildfire smoke from volcanic haze (vog); a plume drifting from Kīlauea, often southwest past Ka Lae on trade winds, is usually vog. Detections inside the Kīlauea and Mauna Loa volcanic zones are suppressed. Daytime only.
adp.meaning_of_absence: No qualifying satellite detection. Does NOT mean there is no haze or smoke.

evidence: no plume localised by Muse Spark or segmented by SAM
result.caveats: No plume found; nothing to classify.

overall.rule: most hazardous class with confidence >= 0.70 (wildfire_smoke > vog_* > dust > cloud)
